async def act(page):
    # Step 1: Search for Covid-related projects
    search_box = page.get_by_role("searchbox", name="Filter by name")
    await search_box.fill("Covid")
    await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)  # Wait for results to update
    
    # Step 2: Check if any projects are displayed after search
    # Use get_by_role to find project headings in the main area
    main_area = page.get_by_role("main")
    project_headings = main_area.get_by_role("heading", level=2)
    count = await project_headings.count()
    if count == 0:
        # No Covid projects found, try searching for 'location tracker'
        await search_box.fill("location tracker")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)
        project_headings = main_area.get_by_role("heading", level=2)
        count = await project_headings.count()
        if count == 0:
            # Still no results, try 'tracker'
            await search_box.fill("tracker")
            await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)
            project_headings = main_area.get_by_role("heading", level=2)
            count = await project_headings.count()
            if count == 0:
                # No relevant projects found, return a message
                return "No Covid location tracker projects found."
    
    # Step 3: Identify the project with the highest star count
    max_stars = -1
    project_name = ""
    for i in range(count):
        heading = project_headings.nth(i)
        # Get the project name from the heading link
        heading_link = heading.get_by_role("link")
        name = await heading_link.inner_text()
        # Find the star count link associated with this project
        # In the tree, star counts are links with numbers; they are siblings under the same parent
        # Use get_by_role to find links with numeric names that are likely star counts
        # We'll look for links that follow the heading and have a numeric inner text
        # This is an approximation; we rely on the structure from the accessibility tree
        # Get all links in the main area after the heading
        all_links = main_area.get_by_role("link")
        star_link = None
        for j in range(await all_links.count()):
            link = all_links.nth(j)
            link_text = await link.inner_text()
            if link_text.isdigit():
                # Check if this link is related to the current project by proximity
                # Since we can't use XPath, we assume the first numeric link after the heading is the star count
                # This might be error-prone but fits the tree structure
                star_link = link
                break
        if star_link:
            star_text = await star_link.inner_text()
            try:
                stars = int(star_text)
                if stars > max_stars:
                    max_stars = stars
                    project_name = name
            except ValueError:
                pass
    
    if not project_name:
        return "Could not determine the most stared project."
    
    # Step 4: Click on the project heading link to navigate to details
    project_link = page.get_by_role("link", name=project_name, exact=True)
    await project_link.click()
    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
    
    # Step 5: Find the SSH clone command on the project details page
    # Look for a textbox with label or specific text
    clone_ssh_element = page.get_by_role("textbox", name="Clone with SSH").or_(page.get_by_text("git@", exact=False))
    if await clone_ssh_element.count() > 0:
        clone_command = await clone_ssh_element.input_value()
    else:
        # Fallback: look for any element containing SSH URL
        ssh_elements = page.get_by_text("git@", exact=False)
        if await ssh_elements.count() > 0:
            clone_command = await ssh_elements.first.inner_text()
        else:
            clone_command = "SSH clone command not found."
    
    return clone_command
